finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.untrusted_source: The PID of the parent process
finding.trigger: If the PID of the parent process is manipulated, it could lead to unintended signal delivery to another process
finding.assumptions: The PID of the parent process is not controlled by an attacker. The parent process is trusted.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Verified that the source of the PID is obtained via the system call getppid(), which returns the actual parent process ID of the calling process and is not influenced by external user input or attacker-controlled data. Since getppid() is a trusted kernel call, there is no untrusted data path leading into kill(). Additionally, kill() is used solely to signal the parent process itself, and no command construction or external input is involved. No checks are needed because the API usage is inherently safe for this context.
